remarks: Every *.jk.gov.in host tried this session (singlewindow.jk.gov.in, law.jk.gov.in, rgp.jk.gov.in, jk.gov.in, www.jk.gov.in) failed identically: the proxy's HTTPS CONNECT tunnel succeeds, but the TLS handshake itself is reset ('Recv failure: Connection reset by peer') immediately after the ClientHello, reproduced on repeated retries and confirmed with curl -v. This is the domain actually hosting J&K's Factory License single-window portal, its checklist/SOP/renewal PDFs, and the state's Factories Rules notifications — i.e. almost everything the spec asks this list to prioritize. A WebFetch attempt on the same host failed with a DNS/allowlist-style error, consistent with this being a this-session network restriction rather than the real-world site being down.

Two separate failure modes were observed and are reflected in the exclusion reasons: (a) 'Recv failure: Connection reset by peer' for *.jk.gov.in, labour.gov.in and shramsuvidha.gov.in (reaches the destination/TLS layer, then resets), vs (b) 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 502' for investjk.in and services.india.gov.in (the egress proxy itself declines the host before any TLS). Re-running this task after the *.jk.gov.in and investjk.in domains are added to this environment's allowed network domains would very likely raise the verified-source count substantially, since the search step surfaced a plausible official checklist PDF, SOP PDF, renewal manual and Factories Rules amendment notifications that could not be independently confirmed this session purely for network-access reasons, not because they appear fake or wrong.

Other candidate categories from the spec (state gazette text of the Factories Rules, 1972; the J&K Single Window Act/Rules PDFs; a central NSWS page specific to J&K's factory-license service) were found via search but could not be verified: either the host was unreachable (as above), or (for nsws.gov.in) the only reachable content was a generic login/profile shell with no J&K- or factory-license-specific text.

Two PDFs discovered on a generic cdnbbsr.s3waas.gov.in bucket that search results associated with 'Jammu and Kashmir Factories Rules, 1972' turned out, on actual inspection, to be Union Territory of Ladakh notifications (Ladakh and J&K share the pre-2019 Factories Rules lineage, which appears to be why search conflated them) — flagged as a reminder that a 200 response and a plausible-looking filename are not sufficient verification; the content must be read.
